Title: Calcium supplementation during pregnancy may reduce preterm delivery in high-risk populations
Author: Villar & Repke
Comment: Calcium arm event count (7) is stated verbatim in the Results text ("All seven preterm deliveries in the calcium group"); placebo arm event count (20) is NOT stated verbatim as a count — it is derived from the reported 21.1% of N = 95 (= 20.0) and is corroborated by the text (14 preterm deliveries with complications + 6.3% idiopathic prematurity of 95 = 6; 14 + 6 = 20). Denominators are the analysis Ns from the Table V header (calcium 94 of 95 randomized, placebo 95); the trial states intention-to-treat allocation ("All subjects were included in the treatment group to which they were originally randomized").; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Calcium supplementation, 2.0 gm/day elemental calcium (4 x 500 mg calcium carbonate, OSCAL 500)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)

Title: Calcium Supplementation in Mild Preeclampsia Remote From Term: A Randomized Double-Blind Clinical Trial
Author: Sanchez-Ramos L, Adair CD, Kaunitz AM, Briones DK, Del Valle GO, Delke I
Comment: The paper does NOT report the number of preterm births (<37 weeks) per arm, so no events/totals could be extracted for the planned risk-ratio pooling; only mean gestational age at delivery is available. The statement "Severe preeclampsia led to preterm delivery in 18 of 36 ... and in 19 of 39" refers to the primary severe-preeclampsia endpoint (delivery indication), not to all preterm births, and was therefore not recorded as a preterm-birth event count. No t statistic or exact p value reported for this outcome ("none of the differences were statistically significant").; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Calcium group (2 g/day elemental calcium)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); excluded by outcome classification: does not match the requested outcome/timepoint (meta_analysis_candidate=False)

Recruitment source: University Medical Center antepartum admissions, July 1990 - January 1993
Outcome measurement: Mean gestational age at delivery in completed weeks (± standard deviation)
Outcome variable: Gestational age at delivery (wk) — proxy for preterm birth

Title: A Randomized Controlled Trial of the Effect of Third-Trimester Calcium Supplementation on Maternal Hemodynamic Function
Author: Boggess KA, Samuel L, Schmucker BC, Waters J, Easterling TR
Comment: The paper does NOT report preterm birth before 37 weeks as an event count with per-arm denominators, so no risk ratio can be computed and the planned RR pooling is not supported by this trial. Only median gestational age at delivery (with ranges) is reported, extracted here as a proxy. The narrative mention that "three developed preterm labor and were treated with terbutaline (all placebo)" refers to preterm LABOR among the 5 study non-completers, not to preterm BIRTH, and no denominator for a preterm-birth event is given — it was therefore NOT recorded as an event count. Medians/ranges are for completers only (11 vs 7), not intention-to-treat (12 vs 11); high differential attrition. No effect measure, CI, or test statistic is reported.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Calcium supplementation (1.5 g elemental calcium/day, completers)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); excluded by outcome classification: does not match the requested outcome/timepoint (meta_analysis_candidate=False); mean/SD estimated from median/RANGE via Wan et al. (2014): treatment mean=38.5000 SD=1.8830, control mean=39.0000 SD=1.4658 -- APPROXIMATION, not directly reported
Participant type: Normotensive pregnant women aged 18–35 years, singleton gestation, receiving prenatal care at a university clinic, randomized at 28–31 weeks' gestation
Recruitment source: University of Washington Medical Center Women's Clinic prenatal care population
Outcome measurement: Median (range) weeks of gestation at delivery; compared by Mann-Whitney U test
additional_group_ns: Randomized: calcium n = 12, placebo n = 11; completers analysed: calcium n = 11, placebo n = 7. Five non-completers: 3 developed preterm labor treated with terbutaline (all placebo), 1 noncompliant (placebo), 1 self-discontinued due to side effects (calcium).
